description:
PR #876 test-refactoring review requested by the user on 2026-11-20.

File: test/zaq/agent/attachment_selection_test.exs, Zaq.Agent.AttachmentSelectionDeliveryTest.
Four tests repeat LLM stub startup, scope creation, IntegrationAgent creation, and Executor.run/2.

Extract a focused private fixture helper for that common setup, accepting the script, incoming message, and execution options needed by the existing scenarios. Keep scenario-specific scripts, assertions, destination setup, and authorization choices visible in each test. Reuse existing support helpers rather than creating a generic test framework.

Acceptance: preserve all four tests and their assertions; retain system-actor versus person-actor execution, explicit permission bypass only where already present, real Storage ACL checks and revocation, no incoming-file echo, HTTP failure versus normal completion, final-B selection, exact bytes, recipient/thread identity, and no duplicate uploads/emails. Preserve supervision, unique scopes, isolation, and cleanup. Do not merge direct Mattermost creation with streamed-ingress edit coverage, or SMTP/MIME with persisted-confirmation coverage.
Validation: mix q and the focused attachment selection suite, including all modules in the file. Final validation remains owned by zaq-1lw.13.

Action reuse assessment: not applicable to production operations; this is test-only consolidation using existing public contracts and fixtures. No production API or behavior changes.
Read AGENTS.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/code-quality.md, and docs/conventions.md before implementation. This issue records the requested work; the user's request to create issues is not an implementation or broader test-behavior approval. Follow the existing-test-behavior gate for retiring tests; preserve assertions and map source coverage to its destination.

comments.text: User explicitly approved focused helper extraction while retaining all four delivery tests and every assertion. .31 validated before starting .32. Evidence: four tests duplicate AttachmentSelectionLLMStub.server/start_supervised!, UUID scope, IntegrationAgent.create! and Executor.run; existing IntegrationAgent support already owns configured runtime cleanup, and must remain owner. Private helper will delegate to these APIs, retain exact scenario job strings, accept script/incoming/execution opts, create a unique scope per invocation, and add no permission/actor defaults. Scripts, system/person events, explicit bypass choices, actual Storage grants/revocation and transport assertions stay at call sites. Action reuse not applicable to production operations: test-only reuse; no new lifecycle, Action, tool, dependency, production behavior or E2E/property work.

Coverage map: all four delivery tests retain their exact script, job instructions and incoming message. First email final-B scenario keeps explicit system event/skip_permissions:true, metadata-free lazy handle assertions, denied final redemption then explicit trusted bypass, exact MIME B bytes/caption and no second email. Mattermost final-B scenario keeps system bypass, actual HTTP upload, exact B bytes/name/MIME, selected shared-room/root-bot IDs, acceptance synchronization and no duplicate upload. Empty replacement keeps both normal text and HTTP400 terminal scripts plus incoming file/no-echo assertion. Person scenario keeps explicit person event with no skip_permissions key, actual Storage grant, failed unauthorized whole replacement, successful B redemption, revocation and denied re-redemption/no email. Private run_selection helper only starts supervised LLM stub, generates fresh UUID scope, calls existing IntegrationAgent.create! with original job/tool and Executor.run with caller opts; IntegrationAgent still owns runtime cleanup. No test, property, assertion or transport boundary removed; baseline full file14 PASS (1 property,13 tests).

Implementation/validation complete: entire attachment_selection_test.exs14 PASS (1 property,13 tests), same as baseline. mix q PASS; git diff --check PASS. Standalone AST audit confirms all120 scenario/property/assertion expressions across all three modules are unchanged after helper extraction and formatting. All four delivery tests retained. Net32 lines saved (15 added,47 removed). Logs /tmp/zaq-1lw-32-{before,after,quality}.log; AST audit /tmp/zaq-1lw-32-audit.exs. Prior issues validated sequentially. No production files changed, so numerical production coverage phase and feature E2E authoring are not applicable to this test-only refactor; existing eight focused properties remain exercised. Proceeding to requested final mix precommit with900s timeout. No commit/push.

Final mix precommit uncovered SMTP confirmation integration timeouts outside the six changed files: stale_metadata and selection_failure did not receive delivery_boundary within5000ms. All four scoped isolated suites and per-issue mix q remain passing. Final stale run still in progress; investigating before claiming final-gate completion. No assertion/timeout weakening or production changes. Will reproduce isolated suite after current run to distinguish baseline failure from consolidation interaction.

First final gate completed exit2:12568/12570 checks passed (48/48 doctests,390/390 properties,12130/12132 tests),1 skipped,167 excluded,452.3s. Only failures were unchanged EmailConfirmationIntegrationTest stale_metadata/selection_failure waiting for SMTP boundary. No failing scoped consolidation tests. Reproducing unchanged suite with seed758067; auditing isolation without changing assertions, timeouts or production. Log /tmp/zaq-1lw-consolidation-precommit.log. Final gate not yet passing.

SMTP failures do not reproduce in isolation: unchanged email_confirmation_integration_test.exs4/4 PASS with same final-gate seed758067 in2.6s, with no code/assertion/timeout changes. This supports an order/load-dependent full-suite failure, not yet a proven root cause. Checking all six consolidation files together with SMTP integration under the same seed before rerunning precommit. No new production work or changed test expectations outside approved consolidation scope.
